body_md:
# consensus-search-log

Turns a folder of Consensus.app PDF exports into two identification CSVs that
fill the first two nodes of a PRISMA (or PRISMA-style) identification funnel:

- `01a_identification_all.csv` — one row per (reference, query) hit
- `01c_identification_dedup.csv` — one row per deduplicated reference, with a
  pipe-delimited list of query IDs that each reference was returned by

The skill is chapter-agnostic. The correctness-wedge Chapter 2 pivot is the
first user, but any future search batch (a Chapter 3 methods sweep, a
supervisor-suggested refresh, a Chapter 4 empirical follow-up) can drop new
PDFs into `consensus-queries/query-results/` (or an alternative folder
passed via `--pdf-dir`) and re-run.

## When to use

- After running a Consensus.app search thread and downloading the per-question
  PDF exports.
- When rebuilding an audit trail from scratch after re-running a query batch
  (the extractor is idempotent — safe to re-run over the same PDFs).
- When adding a new retrieval batch for a subsequent search wave.

## Prerequisites

- `.venv\Scripts\python.exe` with `pymupdf` installed (already in the
  workspace `pyproject.toml`).
- Consensus.app PDFs saved with the filename pattern `Q<NN>_<slug>.pdf` in a
  `query-results/` folder alongside a `logs/prisma-logs/` sibling.
- A batch JSON file under `questions/` listing every question in the thread.

## Input layout

```
G:\...\thesis-review-method\consensus-queries\
├── query-results\
│   ├── Q01_<slug>.pdf
│   ├── Q02_<slug>.pdf
│   └── ...
├── abstracts\           (created by fetch_abstracts.py)
└── logs\
    ├── prisma-logs\     (Ch2 PRISMA identification CSVs)
    └── non-prisma-logs\ (chapter-scoped anchor logs)
```

Only the `Q<NN>` prefix on each PDF matters; the rest of the filename is
ignored. Retrieval date lives inside the batch JSON and inside every audit
log filename; a dedicated date-partitioned subfolder is not required.
Future batches can either overwrite the current layout (simplest when there
is one active batch per chapter) or be routed to an alternative folder via
the CLI flags below.

## Question set format

`questions/<batch_id>.json`:

```json
{
  "batch_id": "2026-08-22_correctness-wedge",
  "retrieval_date": "2026-08-22",
  "wave": "CW1",
  "source": "consensus.app",
  "thread_description": "Correctness-wedge sixteen-question thread. Canonical text lives in <path>",
  "questions": [
    {"query_id": "Q01", "text": "To what extent does..."},
    {"query_id": "Q02", "text": "Does the adoption of..."}
  ]
}
```

- `batch_id` — unique identifier; often `<retrieval-date>_<thread-name>`.
- `retrieval_date` — populates the CSV context column.
- `wave` — free-form label; the correctness-wedge batch uses `CW1`.
- `questions[].query_id` — must match the `Q<NN>` prefix on the PDFs.
- `questions[].text` — the exact question text that was posted to Consensus.

Store one JSON file per retrieval batch. The canonical file for the
correctness-wedge Chapter 2 batch is
`questions/2026-08-22_correctness-wedge.json`.

## Pre-processing new retrievals: `rename_consensus_downloads.py`

Consensus PDF exports come pre-named `Q<nn>_<truncated_query>.pdf`, but the
paired CSV downloads land with the full question text as the filename
(with spaces, punctuation, and often exceeding Windows MAX_PATH). Before
running the extractor on a new batch, run this helper to rename the CSVs
into the same `Q<nn>_<truncation>.csv` scheme as the PDFs.

Matching normalises both sides to `[A-Za-z0-9_]` and looks for the PDF
truncation as a prefix of the CSV stem. Ambiguous or unmatched CSVs are
reported and skipped, never renamed automatically. Rename operations use
the Windows extended-length path prefix (`\\?\`) so filenames longer than
260 characters still succeed.

```powershell
# Dry-run against the default paths (correctness-wedge batch):
& ".venv\Scripts\python.exe" `
    ".github\skills\consensus-search-log\scripts\rename_consensus_downloads.py"

# Actually rename:
& ".venv\Scripts\python.exe" `
    ".github\skills\consensus-search-log\scripts\rename_consensus_downloads.py" `
    --apply

# Explicit paths for a future batch:
& ".venv\Scripts\python.exe" `
    ".github\skills\consensus-search-log\scripts\rename_consensus_downloads.py" `
    --pdf-dir "G:\...\<batch>\pdf" `
    --csv-dir "G:\...\<batch>\csv" `
    --apply
```

The script refuses to `--apply` when any CSV is ambiguous or unmatched;
resolve those manually first (typically Consensus renamed the PDF stem
after CSV export, or two PDFs share the same truncation prefix).

## Running the pipeline

Default paths (correctness-wedge Chapter 2 batch):

```powershell
& ".venv\Scripts\python.exe" `
    ".github\skills\consensus-search-log\scripts\extract_consensus_refs.py"
```

Explicit paths (any future batch):

```powershell
& ".venv\Scripts\python.exe" `
    ".github\skills\consensus-search-log\scripts\extract_consensus_refs.py" `
    --pdf-dir "G:\...\consensus-queries\query-results" `
    --questions ".github\skills\consensus-search-log\questions\<batch>.json" `
    --out-dir "G:\...\consensus-queries\logs\prisma-logs"
```

Sanity-check the outputs:

```powershell
& ".venv\Scripts\python.exe" `
    ".github\skills\consensus-search-log\scripts\check_consensus_csvs.py" `
    --logs-dir "G:\...\consensus-queries\logs\prisma-logs"
```

The checker reports per-query counts, top cross-query hits, and any rows
missing a DOI / year / title so gaps can be triaged before the next PRISMA
node.

## CSV schemas

### `01a_identification_all.csv`

One row per (reference, query) hit. A single paper returned by three
queries produces three rows.

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `ref_id` | Global row id, `R0001` upwards, stable across runs when input PDFs unchanged. |
| `query_id` | `Q01`..`Q<NN>`, matching the PDF prefix. |
| `wave` | From the batch JSON. |
| `retrieval_date` | From the batch JSON. |
| `query_text` | The full question the reference was returned by. |
| `refs_returned_in_query` | Count of references parsed from that query's PDF; the PRISMA "records identified" grain. |
| `consensus_meter_n` | The N reported by Consensus's meter, when the meter appears; blank when the PDF shows "Requires at least 5 papers" instead. |
| `authors` | APA author-list string as printed in the PDF. |
| `year` | 4-digit year (with optional letter suffix). |
| `title` | Paper title, punctuation preserved. |
| `venue` | Journal, conference proceedings, or preprint server (e.g. `ArXiv, abs/2506.08945`). |
| `doi_url` | Full `https://doi.org/...` URL as printed. Empty for entries without a DOI. |
| `notes` | Reserved for human annotations after the identification step. |

### `01c_identification_dedup.csv`

One row per deduplicated reference.

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `unique_ref_id` | Global unique id, `U0001` upwards. |
| `hit_count` | Number of queries that returned this reference. |
| `query_ids` | Pipe-delimited list of `Q<NN>` values (sorted, unique). |
| `authors`, `year`, `title`, `venue`, `doi_url` | Same as identification CSV, sourced from the first hit encountered. |
| `dedup_key` | The key used for deduplication (`doi:<canonical>` or `title:<slug>|year:<yyyy>`); kept for audit. |
| `track2_status` | Blank for records that go forward to title+abstract screening. Stamped with the matching Track 2 `anchor_id` (e.g. `T2-B03`) when the record's canonical DOI matches a row in `01b_identification_track2_anchors.csv`. Cross-track duplicates are excluded from screening because they are already reviewed under the Track 2 purposive-selection arm. |
| `notes` | Reserved for human annotations. |

## Deduplication logic

1. **DOI-first (within Track 1).** DOIs are canonicalised: strip `https://`,
   `dx.`, and `doi.org/`; lowercase; trim trailing punctuation. Two Track 1
   records with the same canonical DOI collapse into one.
2. **Title + year fallback (within Track 1).** For records without a DOI,
   the title is Unicode-normalised (NFKD), stripped of non-alphanumeric
   characters, and lower-cased; the year is appended. Identical normalised
   keys collapse.
3. **Cross-track dedup (Track 1 vs Track 2).** After Track 1 dedup, each
   surviving row's canonical DOI is compared against the DOI column of
   `01b_identification_track2_anchors.csv`. Matches are kept in the CSV but
   tagged in the new `track2_status` column with the Track 2 `anchor_id`.
   The downstream `fetch_abstracts.py` skips tagged rows (no API calls,
   `abstract_location` set to `track2_anchor:<anchor_id>`), and the
   title+abstract screening step ignores them because they are already
   under review as full-paper anchors.

Cross-query hits are captured by the `query_ids` list on the surviving row.
When two rows for the same paper collapse, the `authors` / `title` / `venue`
values come from the first row encountered (sorted by `query_id`, then
author). If those values diverge across the source hits (rare — Consensus
usually returns identical APA strings for the same DOI), the divergence is
lost; log it in `notes` if manual fix-up matters.

## Consensus PDF quirks worth knowing

- **Meter versus References count.** When Consensus renders the meter (`N =
  X`), the meter's N is a filtered sub-count and is often smaller than the
  number of references actually listed. The PRISMA "records identified"
  grain is the References-section count (`refs_returned_in_query`), not the
  meter's N.
- **"Requires at least 5 papers" queries.** For thin queries, Consensus
  shows a message instead of a meter. `consensus_meter_n` stays blank; the
  References section still lists whatever the model surfaced.
- **DOI URL variants.** Consensus mixes `https://doi.org/10.xxxx/...` with
  arXiv-DOI proxies (`https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.<id>`) and SSRN
  (`https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.<id>`). All are treated as valid DOIs and
  contribute to the dedup key.
- **Books without a DOI.** Rare, but they appear when Consensus surfaces
  seminal texts. The title-plus-year fallback catches them; the row will
  need manual DOI lookup at Zotero import time.

## Downstream

The `01c_identification_dedup.csv` file is the handoff artefact for the
next PRISMA node (title-and-abstract screening). Under the correctness-wedge
pivot, that screening runs against the Chapter 2 IC/EC rubric — see the
Chapter 2 decision memo at
`G:\...\correctness-wedge\thesis-review-method\ch2-review-form-decision-memo.md`
for the shape of that rubric under the "structured, theory-anchored review"
choice.

For a fuller LLM-adjudication pipeline (used if the review returns to a
formal PRISMA systematic-review form), see the `lit-screening` skill, which
consumes a JSONL representation of the deduped records.

## Fetching titles and abstracts

`scripts/fetch_abstracts.py` enriches every row of the dedup CSV with a
markdown file containing the paper's title and abstract, and adds an
`abstract_location` column to the CSV pointing at that file. This gives the
title-and-abstract screening step a self-contained corpus keyed by
`unique_ref_id`, without a live network dependency.

### Sources and waterfall

For each reference the fetcher tries sources in this uniform order and stops
as soon as an abstract is obtained:

1. **Crossref** — the citation-of-record for publisher DOIs. Provides the
   title, venue, and (when the publisher submits one) a JATS abstract.
   Returns 404 quickly for arXiv-proxy DOIs, so it is cheap to try first for
   every row.
2. **Semantic Scholar** — broad abstract coverage; keyed by DOI or arXiv
   ID. Requires `S2_API_KEY` in `.env`. See the preprint-cluster caveat
   below.
3. **OpenAlex** — aggregates Crossref, PubMed, arXiv, and other sources.
   Abstracts arrive as a positional inverted index and are reconstructed on
   the fly. No API key needed; polite pool uses the `mailto` parameter from
   `CROSSREF_MAILTO`.
4. **arXiv** — authoritative for preprints (`10.48550/arxiv.<id>` DOIs).
   Only queried when the DOI is in the arXiv proxy namespace.

Title and venue are filled from the first source that supplies each; abstract
from the first source that supplies it. A per-reference "fetch trace" is
written into the markdown so a reviewer can see which source answered which
field.

### Rate limits

- Crossref polite pool: 1 req/sec self-imposed (Crossref allows 50/sec but
  the workload is small).
- Semantic Scholar (with API key): 1 req/sec.
- OpenAlex polite pool: 1 req/sec self-imposed (OpenAlex allows 10/sec but
  the workload is small). No API key; the `mailto` parameter identifies the
  caller.
- arXiv: 1 req per 3 sec, per arXiv's published guideline.

Enforcement is per-host inside the script via a monotonic-clock rate
limiter.

### Audit logging

Every run writes a timestamped audit log to `--log-dir` (default
`logs/consensus-search-log/` at the workspace root, gitignored). Filename:
`fetch_abstracts_<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>.log`. The log records each source call
with its outcome (took title/abstract/venue, or the specific error), the
cached-vs-fresh decision per row, and the run summary. Progress lines still
stream to stdout during the run; the file is the persistent audit trail for
diagnosing failures after the fact.

### Environment variables

`.env` at the workspace root (gitignored):

```
S2_API_KEY=<your Semantic Scholar key>
CROSSREF_MAILTO=<contact email for the polite pool>
```

A committed template lives at `.env.example`. If `S2_API_KEY` is absent, the
fetcher continues but Semantic Scholar calls run unauthenticated and may
throttle.

### Output layout

```
G:\...\consensus-queries\abstracts\
├── U0001_<year>_<first-author-surname>.md
├── U0002_<year>_<first-author-surname>.md
└── ...
```

Filename shape: `<unique_ref_id>_<year>_<slug(first-author-surname)>.md`.
The slug is Unicode-normalised (NFKD), stripped of non-alphanumeric
characters, and lower-cased.

Markdown body:

```markdown
# <Title>

- unique_ref_id: U0001
- authors: <APA string>
- year: <year>
- venue: <venue>
- doi: <DOI URL>
- hit_count: <int>
- query_ids: <Q01|Q02|...>
- fetched_at: <UTC timestamp>

## Abstract

<abstract text or a placeholder if not retrieved>

## Provenance

- Title source: <crossref|semantic-scholar|arxiv|consensus-csv>
- Abstract source: <crossref|semantic-scholar|arxiv|none>
- [Semantic-Scholar caveat line, only when Abstract source is semantic-scholar]
- Fetch trace:
  - crossref: took title+abstract+venue
  - semantic-scholar: skipped
```

### Semantic Scholar preprint-cluster caveat

Semantic Scholar clusters preprint and published versions of the same paper
under a single record and stores one canonical abstract per record. When the
fetcher retrieves an abstract via Semantic Scholar for a publisher DOI, that
abstract may originate from a preprint version and may not match the
publisher-registered abstract of the version of record.

The fetcher handles this in two ways:

- **In the markdown Provenance block.** When `Abstract source:
  semantic-scholar`, an extra line is written directly under the source
  attribution, warning the reviewer that the abstract may be preprint-
  sourced and should be verified against the publisher-side abstract before
  the paper is cited in the thesis.
- **In the dedup CSV.** A boolean column `abstract_from_s2_cluster` records
  the same information at row level so a screening spreadsheet can filter or
  sort on it. Values: `True` when the abstract came from Semantic Scholar,
  `False` when it came from Crossref or arXiv, and blank when no abstract
  was retrieved (unavailable rows).

ArXiv-DOI'd papers are unaffected: their DOI itself declares them as
preprints, so there is no substitution risk to flag.

### `abstract_location` and `abstract_from_s2_cluster` columns

After a run, the dedup CSV gains two new columns (inserted before `notes`):

- `abstract_location`. Forward-slash relative path from the CSV to the
  markdown (e.g. `../abstracts/U0001_2026_agarwal.md`), or the literal
  string `unavailable` when no source supplied an abstract. Unavailable
  rows do not get a markdown file.
- `abstract_from_s2_cluster`. `True` when the abstract was sourced from
  Semantic Scholar (may be preprint-sourced; see caveat above), `False`
  when it came from Crossref or arXiv, blank when the row is unavailable.

### Running the fetcher

Defaults (correctness-wedge 2026-08-22 batch):

```powershell
& ".venv\Scripts\python.exe" `
    ".github\skills\consensus-search-log\scripts\fetch_abstracts.py"
```

Useful flags:

- `--dedup-csv <path>` — point at a different batch's dedup CSV.
- `--out-dir <path>` — override the `abstracts/` sibling folder.
- `--limit N` — process only the first N rows (handy for smoke tests).
- `--force` — refetch even when a markdown file already exists (default is
  cache-and-skip).
- `--env-file <path>` — non-default `.env` location.
- `--log-dir <path>` — override the audit-log folder.

The fetcher is idempotent. On re-runs, a reference whose markdown already
exists is left alone (only its CSV cell is refreshed); passing `--force`
overwrites the markdown too. Rows currently marked `unavailable` in the CSV
have no markdown file and will be re-attempted on a plain re-run — useful
when adding a new source to the waterfall (as with the OpenAlex addition).

### CSV write failures

If the dedup CSV is open in Excel while the fetcher runs, the atomic
rename at the end fails. The updated data is left at
`01c_identification_dedup.csv.tmp` next to the original; close Excel and
rename manually.

## History

  206 unique references, 39 duplicates removed).

  Semantic Scholar / arXiv waterfall over
  `01c_identification_dedup.csv`, writes one markdown per hit under the
  batch's `abstracts/` folder, and populates the new `abstract_location`
  column.
- 2026-09-01 — Semantic Scholar preprint-cluster caveat added. Markdown
  Provenance blocks now carry a warning line when the abstract came from
  Semantic Scholar, and the dedup CSV gained an `abstract_from_s2_cluster`
  boolean column recording the same signal at row level.
- 2026-09-01 — OpenAlex added as a fallback source and the waterfall
  reordered to Crossref → Semantic Scholar → OpenAlex → arXiv uniformly.
  File-based audit logging under `logs/consensus-search-log/` was added so
  every source call is recorded to a timestamped log file for later
  diagnosis.
- 2026-09-02 — file-naming schema swapped and cross-track dedup added.
  `01c_identification_track2_anchors.csv` renamed to
  `01b_identification_track2_anchors.csv`; `01b_identification_dedup.csv`
  renamed to `01c_identification_dedup.csv`. The alphabetical order now
  reflects PRISMA processing order: Track 2 anchors are established first
  (01b), then Track 1 dedup runs against them (01c). `extract_consensus_refs.py`
  gained a `--track2-csv` argument and a new `track2_status` column on the
  dedup CSV that stamps each row with a matching Track 2 `anchor_id`.
  `fetch_abstracts.py` skips tagged rows and records
  `abstract_location = track2_anchor:<anchor_id>` for audit. This prevents
  Track 2 anchors from being re-screened at the title+abstract step under

- 2026-09-02 — stable-key markdown filenames and screening-exclusion skip.
  `fetch_abstracts.py` no longer keys the markdown filename on the
  positional `unique_ref_id` (which shifts every time new Consensus queries
  are added and the dedup sort re-orders). Filenames are now
  `{year}_{surname}_{dedup8}.md` where `dedup8` is an 8-hex-char MD5 of the
  row's stable `dedup_key`. Re-runs after adding new queries treat existing
  files as cache hits and only fetch new rows. The fetcher also loads
  `2b_screening_excluded.csv` and skips any row whose canonical DOI matches
  the exclude list, recording `abstract_location = excluded:<reason>` for
  audit without making API calls. Downstream title+abstract screening
  therefore never re-encounters explicitly-excluded references. Stale files
  from newly-excluded rows are moved into `abstracts/_orphans/` for audit
  when the exclude list grows.
- 2026-09-02 — CSV log integrity discipline codified. New
  `.github/instructions/csv-log-discipline.instructions.md` governs all six
  logs (`01a`, `01b`, `01c`, `2b`, `ch3_methods_anchors`, `signpost_citations`)
  and their linked corpora (abstract markdowns and Track 2 decision
  markdowns). Every log now carries a `stable_id` column (8-hex MD5 of the
  row's identity key) that survives Consensus batch expansion and
  re-sorts; the human-readable ID column (`ref_id`, `unique_ref_id`,
  `anchor_id`, `signpost_id`) is retained for display only. Manual IDs
  (`T2-*`, `CH3-*`, `SG-*`) are immutable once assigned. New
  `scripts/csv_lint.py` enforces stable_id uniqueness, cross-log referential
  integrity, and both corpus contracts; it must exit zero before any
  commit touching these paths. `fetch_abstracts.py` and
  `extract_consensus_refs.py` acquire a `.pid` lockfile on their target CSV
  and refuse to start if another live process holds it, preventing the
  double-writer race that produced the 2026-09-02 orphan-file fiasco.
  `logs-index.csv` grew `unique_id_column`, `id_derivation`, and
  `robustness_class` columns so the manifest itself documents each log's
  identifier contract.

- 2026-09-02 — manual-abstract overlay. New `manual_abstracts.csv` under
